sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Immunofluorescence in HEK293 and HepG2 cells confirmed correct localization to endocytic/endosomal compartments (co-staining with Rab27-GFP). C-terminal tagging was explicitly shown to be non-functional, validating the N-terminal position as the functional configuration.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the 3xFLAG tag was engineered 'at amino acid position 28, immediately after the signal peptide.' The signal peptide spans residues 1–27 (last residue A at position 27), so insert_after_residue=27 places the tag between A(27) and D(28), the mature N-terminus. Python verification confirms seq[26]='A' and seq[27]='D'. L2 corroborates the junction and explains that C-terminal tagging is non-functional, making this the only validated surface-accessible position. L3 confirms the construct was used in functional localization assays. Full-length membrane-anchored human RNF130 with a 3xFLAG tag engineered immediately after the signal peptide (residues 1–27), placing the tag at the mature N-terminus (residue 28). Construct expressed in HEK293 and HepG2 cells and used for immunofluorescence localization studies with endosomal markers.

sources.claim: Human RNF130 was also generated with a 3xFLAG epitope engineered at amino acid position 28 after the signal peptide as a double-stranded DNA gBlock (IDT Technologies).

literature_notes: Three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) all describe the same construct and junction: 3xFLAG inserted after the signal peptide cleavage site (after residue 27, before the mature D28). L2 explicitly disqualifies C-terminal tagging as non-functional. The second extracellular span (residues 406–419, 14 aa) is topologically surface-exposed but no ledger line supports an insertion there, and L2's statement about C-terminal non-functionality covers any tag at or near the C-terminus. No other internal extracellular loop insertions are reported in the ledger for RNF130.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal tagging of RNF130 renders the protein non-functional (data shown in the paper); the authors switched to N-terminal tagging after the signal peptide for all functional studies.
